`qaqcmar` applies quality control flags to Water Quality data collected
through the Centre for Marine Applied Research’s (CMAR) [Coastal
Monitoring Program](https://cmar.ca/coastal-monitoring-program/).

## Installation

You can install the development version of `qaqcmar` from
[GitHub](https://github.com/) with:

``` r
# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("centre-for-marine-applied-research/qaqcmar")
```

`qaqcmar` uses the CMAR-developed
[`sensorstrings`](https://github.com/centre-for-marine-applied-research/sensorstrings)
package (version 1.4.1 or later), which is installed automatically.

See [NEWS.md](NEWS.md) for the changes in each version. Version 2.0.0
changes some arguments and the format of the threshold and human in the
loop tables.

## Background

### Coastal Monitoring Program

The Centre for Marine Applied Research ([CMAR](https://cmar.ca/))
coordinates an extensive [Coastal Monitoring
Program](https://cmar.ca/coastal-monitoring-program/) to measure
[Essential Ocean
Variables](https://www.goosocean.org/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=14&Itemid=114)
from around the coast of Nova Scotia, Canada. There are three main
branches of the program: *Water Quality*, *Currents*, and *Waves*.
Summary reports and full datasets for each branch can be viewed and
downloaded from several sources, as outlined in the [CMAR Data Access
Reference
Sheet](https://cmar.ca/wp-content/uploads/sites/22/2026/10/2026-10-13_data_access_ns.pdf).

### Quality Assurance and Quality Control

CMAR applies Quality Assurance (QA) and Quality Control (QC) processes
to support the delivery of high quality data (Bushnell et al., 2019). QA
processes are typically completed prior to sensor deployment (e.g.,
sensor calibration and validation), and are documented in a series of
Standard Operating Procedures.

QC processes (e.g., automated data flags, manual review) are completed
for each deployment after the data have been collected and compiled.
CMAR has adapted the QARTOD (Quality Assurance / Quality Control of
Real-Time Oceanographic Data) flagging scheme and associated tests.
QARTOD provides a relatively simple yet informative rating scale, and is
very well documented. QARTOD manuals provide codeable instructions for
implementing recommended QC tests. QARTOD has been adopted by
oceanographic organizations around the world, including the US
Integrated Ocean Observing System (IOOS).

For more information on the QC tests and thresholds, visit the [CMAR
Data Governance
Website](https://centre-for-marine-applied-research.github.io/cmp-data-governance/pages/cmp_about.html).

### Flags

Each test gives every observation one of four flags:

| Flag | Label | Meaning |
|----|----|----|
| 1 | Pass | The observation passed the test. |
| 2 | Not Evaluated | The test could not be applied (e.g., no thresholds for the variable, or not enough nearby observations). |
| 3 | Suspect/Of Interest | The observation is unusual. It may be poor quality, or it may be a real event. |
| 4 | Fail | The observation is very likely poor quality. |

### Tests

| Test | Function | What it checks |
|----|----|----|
| Gross range | `qc_test_grossrange()` | The observation is within the sensor’s range and within a reasonable range for the variable. |
| Climatology | `qc_test_climatology()` | The observation is within the expected range for the variable and month. |
| Spike | `qc_test_spike()` | The observation is not much higher or lower than the observations on either side of it. |
| Rolling standard deviation | `qc_test_rolling_sd()` | The standard deviation of the observations in a rolling window (default 24 hours) is not unusually high. |
| Depth crosscheck | `qc_test_depth_crosscheck()` | The minimum measured depth of each sensor is close to its estimated depth (`sensor_depth_at_low_tide_m`). One flag for each deployment. |
| Human in the loop | `qc_test_human_in_loop()` | Flags assigned by a person after reviewing the automated flags. |

The default thresholds for each test are in the `thresholds` table. Most
depend on the county where the data were collected, and some also depend
on the sensor type or month.

## Example

``` r
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
library(qaqcmar)
library(sensorstrings)
```

### Example data

Consider simulated Water Quality data from January 1 to December 28,
2023, recorded by four sensors in Lunenburg County. (Note: these data
were simulated to illustrate quality control processes and do not
reflect expected profiles.)

``` r
path <- system.file("testdata", package = "qaqcmar")

dat <- readRDS(file.path(path, "test_data_grossrange.RDS"))

kable(dat[1:5, ])
```

| Lunenburg | White Tower | 2023-Jan-01 to 2023-Dec-28 | aquameasure | 456 | 5 | 2023-01-01 | -5 | -60 |
| Lunenburg | White Tower | 2023-Jan-01 to 2023-Dec-28 | aquameasure | 456 | 5 | 2023-02-01 | -5 | -60 |

| Lunenburg | White Tower | 2023-Jan-01 to 2023-Dec-28 | aquameasure | 456 | 5 | 2023-04-01 | -5 | -60 |

### Apply one test

`qaqcmar` includes a separate function for each QC test. For example,
`qc_test_grossrange()` applies the gross range test by adding a
`grossrange_flag_<variable>` column for each variable in `dat`. The
county is taken from the `county` column of `dat`, or can be given with
the `county` argument.

``` r
dat_gr <- qc_test_grossrange(dat, county = "Lunenburg")

kable(dat_gr[1:5, ])
```

| county | station | deployment_range | sensor_type | sensor_serial_number | timestamp_utc | sensor_depth_at_low_tide_m | dissolved_oxygen_percent_saturation | temperature_degree_c | grossrange_flag_dissolved_oxygen_percent_saturation | grossrange_flag_temperature_degree_c |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|---:|:---|---:|---:|---:|:---|:---|
| Lunenburg | White Tower | 2023-Jan-01 to 2023-Dec-28 | aquameasure | 456 | 2023-01-01 | 5 | -5 | -60 | 4 | 4 |
| Lunenburg | White Tower | 2023-Jan-01 to 2023-Dec-28 | aquameasure | 456 | 2023-02-01 | 5 | -5 | -60 | 4 | 4 |
| Lunenburg | White Tower | 2023-Jan-01 to 2023-Dec-28 | aquameasure | 456 | 2023-03-01 | 5 | -5 | -60 | 4 | 4 |
| Lunenburg | White Tower | 2023-Jan-01 to 2023-Dec-28 | aquameasure | 456 | 2023-04-01 | 5 | -5 | -60 | 4 | 4 |
| Lunenburg | White Tower | 2023-Jan-01 to 2023-Dec-28 | aquameasure | 456 | 2023-05-01 | 5 | -5 | -60 | 4 | 4 |

`qc_plot_flags()` returns a list of figures, coloured by flag, with one
element for each variable and, within it, one for each test in
`qc_tests`.

``` r
p <- qc_plot_flags(dat_gr, qc_tests = "grossrange", ncol = 2)

p$temperature_degree_c$grossrange
```

<img src="man/figures/README-fig2-1.png" alt="" width="100%" />

### Apply several tests

`qc_test_all()` applies the tests in `qc_tests` and returns one flag
column for each test and variable. Here, all five automated tests are
applied.

``` r
dat2 <- readRDS(file.path(path, "test_data_rolling_sd.RDS"))

dat_qc <- dat2 |>
  qc_test_all(
    qc_tests = c(
      "climatology",
      "depth_crosscheck",
      "grossrange",
      "rolling_sd",
      "spike"
    )
  )

colnames(dat_qc)
#>  [1] "county"                                              
#>  [2] "waterbody"                                           
#>  [3] "station"                                             
#>  [4] "deployment_range"                                    
#>  [5] "sensor_type"                                         
#>  [6] "sensor_serial_number"                                
#>  [7] "timestamp_utc"                                       
#>  [8] "sensor_depth_at_low_tide_m"                          
#>  [9] "depth_crosscheck_flag"                               
#> [10] "dissolved_oxygen_percent_saturation"                 
#> [11] "sensor_depth_measured_m"                             
#> [12] "climatology_flag_dissolved_oxygen_percent_saturation"
#> [13] "climatology_flag_sensor_depth_measured_m"            
#> [14] "grossrange_flag_dissolved_oxygen_percent_saturation" 
#> [15] "grossrange_flag_sensor_depth_measured_m"             
#> [16] "rolling_sd_flag_dissolved_oxygen_percent_saturation" 
#> [17] "rolling_sd_flag_sensor_depth_measured_m"             
#> [18] "spike_flag_dissolved_oxygen_percent_saturation"      
#> [19] "spike_flag_sensor_depth_measured_m"
```

`qc_assign_max_flag()` adds a `qc_flag_<variable>` column with the
*worst* flag for each observation of each variable. The depth crosscheck
flag is not included, because it is one value for the whole deployment.

``` r
dat_qc <- qc_assign_max_flag(dat_qc)

kable(dat_qc[
  1:5,
  c(
    "timestamp_utc",
    "dissolved_oxygen_percent_saturation",
    "qc_flag_dissolved_oxygen_percent_saturation"
  )
])
```

| timestamp_utc | dissolved_oxygen_percent_saturation | qc_flag_dissolved_oxygen_percent_saturation |
|:---|---:|:---|
| 2023-01-01 12:00:00 | 100.0000 | 2 |
| 2023-01-01 12:30:00 | 100.2611 | 2 |
| 2023-01-01 13:00:00 | 100.5176 | 2 |
| 2023-01-01 13:30:00 | 100.7654 | 2 |
| 2023-01-01 14:00:00 | 101.0000 | 2 |

`qc_summarise_flags()` counts the observations with each flag.

``` r
dat_qc |>
  qc_summarise_flags() |>
  filter(qc_test == "qc", variable == "dissolved_oxygen_percent_saturation") |>
  kable()
```

| qc_test | variable | flag_value | n_flag | n_percent |

| qc | dissolved_oxygen_percent_saturation | Not Evaluated | 47 | 4.66 |
| qc | dissolved_oxygen_percent_saturation | Suspect/Of Interest | 693 | 68.68 |

## Thresholds

To see the default thresholds for a test, filter the `thresholds` table.
Rows with `county = NA` apply in every county.

``` r
thresholds |>
  filter(
    qc_test == "grossrange",
    variable == "temperature_degree_c",
    is.na(county) | county == "Lunenburg"
  ) |>
  kable()
```

| qc_test | variable | county | month | sensor_type | threshold | threshold_value |
|:---|:---|:---|---:|:---|:---|---:|
| grossrange | temperature_degree_c | NA | NA | aquameasure | sensor_min | -55.000 |
| grossrange | temperature_degree_c | NA | NA | aquameasure | sensor_max | 125.000 |
| grossrange | temperature_degree_c | NA | NA | hobo | sensor_min | -40.000 |
| grossrange | temperature_degree_c | NA | NA | hobo | sensor_max | 70.000 |
| grossrange | temperature_degree_c | NA | NA | hobo do | sensor_min | -5.000 |
| grossrange | temperature_degree_c | NA | NA | hobo do | sensor_max | 40.000 |
| grossrange | temperature_degree_c | NA | NA | vr2ar | sensor_min | -5.000 |
| grossrange | temperature_degree_c | NA | NA | vr2ar | sensor_max | 40.000 |
| grossrange | temperature_degree_c | NA | NA | tidbit | sensor_min | -20.000 |
| grossrange | temperature_degree_c | NA | NA | tidbit | sensor_max | 50.000 |
| grossrange | temperature_degree_c | Lunenburg | NA | NA | user_min | -7.269 |
| grossrange | temperature_degree_c | Lunenburg | NA | NA | user_max | 21.551 |

Each test also accepts a table of thresholds, e.g., `grossrange_table`
for `qc_test_grossrange()`. A user table has a `variable` column and one
column for each threshold, and optionally `sensor_type` and `month`
columns. An `NA` in `sensor_type` or `month` (or no column) means the
row applies to any sensor type or month. A sensor-specific row is used
before an “any sensor” row.

``` r
my_grossrange <- data.frame(
  variable = "temperature_degree_c",
  sensor_type = c(NA, "vr2ar"),
  sensor_min = c(-5, -5),
  sensor_max = c(35, 40),
  user_min = c(-1, 0),
  user_max = c(25, 20)
)

dat_user <- qc_test_grossrange(dat, grossrange_table = my_grossrange)
```

## Human in the loop

After reviewing the automated flags, a person can assign flags with
`qc_test_human_in_loop()`. Each row of `human_in_loop_table` flags the
observations of one deployment:

- `variable` and `sensor_serial_number`: the variable and sensor to flag
  (`NA` flags every variable or every sensor).
- `timestamp_utc_min` and `timestamp_utc_max`: the first and last
  observation to flag (`NA` means the start or end of the deployment).
- `qc_test` and `qc_flag_value` (optional): only flag observations that
  this test gave this flag.
- `human_in_loop_flag_value` and `hil_comment`: the flag and comment to
  assign.

Rows for other deployments are ignored, so the whole table can be passed
for every deployment.

``` r
hil_table <- data.frame(
  station = "lighthouse",
  deployment_range = "2023-Jan-01 to 2023-Jan-15",
  variable = "dissolved_oxygen_percent_saturation",
  sensor_serial_number = NA,
  timestamp_utc_min = as.POSIXct("2023-01-15 12:30", tz = "UTC"),
  timestamp_utc_max = NA,
  qc_test = "rolling_sd",
  qc_flag_value = 3,
  human_in_loop_flag_value = 4,
  hil_comment = "dissolved oxygen: biofouling"
)

dat_hil <- dat2 |>
  qc_test_rolling_sd() |>
  qc_test_human_in_loop(hil_table)

dat_hil |>
  count(human_in_loop_flag_dissolved_oxygen_percent_saturation, hil_comment) |>
  kable()
```

| human_in_loop_flag_dissolved_oxygen_percent_saturation | hil_comment | n |
|:---|:---|---:|
| 1 | NA | 697 |
| 4 | dissolved oxygen: biofouling | 312 |
